items.chosen: single augmented LLM call | fixed workflow | autonomous agent | multi-agent system | single augmented LLM call
items.keyed: single augmented LLM call | fixed workflow | autonomous agent | multi-agent system | single augmented LLM call
items.reasoning: Structured extraction with retrieval = augmented call; repeatable filing = workflow; path depends on each result = agent; parallel specialist assessments = multi-agent; glossary rewrite = augmented call.
Error cost is the binding constraint in the five-factor test and selects the workflow regardless of the permissive factors.
Unreconstructable diagnostic paths under regulatory error cost is a pattern mismatch, not just a logging gap.
Fixed workflow is indicated by per-step auditability and by steps known in advance and identical each run.
Balances and outage state are live system-of-record state; they must be read by tool call at request time, not indexed.
Frequently-edited documentary content is the canonical retrieval-augmentation case.
Two distinct weaknesses map to two distinct patterns; routing does not fix layout-driven extraction failure.
Multi-agent is warranted by specialisation that would overload one agent and by parallelisable independent sub-tasks.
Ordered determination record plus a hard halt requires supervisor orchestration, not peer handoffs or instructed self-sequencing.
Skipped criteria after two prompt rewrites is a task-complexity ceiling; decompose into sequenced subtasks.
Tool-selection accuracy falling as surface grows is the split-behind-a-router signal.
First use case is chosen on measurable business value and feasible data access with manageable risk.
Clinician corrections already exist as ground truth; capturing them into a labelled eval set closes the quality-measurement gap.
Start on the default mid tier and treat any tier move as a release gated by an eval set and rollback criterion.
Hand-picked eyeballing is not evidence; a tier swap needs a defined eval set and a pre-agreed rollback criterion.
Where accuracy is equivalent across the family and latency/cost matter, take the smallest model meeting the target and keep evaluating.
Loading everything every request is monolithic context; the fix is progressive context per step.
A request id and timestamp at the head of the prompt change the prefix every call, so no cache prefix can match.
Chain-of-thought pays on multi-step reasoning only; apply per task on measured benefit.
A rule buried mid-prompt in reference material needs boundary placement and structural separation of rules from reference.
Single-category examples narrowed behaviour; the example set is unrepresentative of the real input distribution.
Retrieve only relevant sections and chunk on structural boundaries: fixes both lost-in-the-middle and cost.
Cacheable static prefix plus on-demand modular instructions cut per-request cost without losing capability.
Contradictory rules need delimited sections with explicit priority, plus examples of correct handling.
End-user identity propagation and least-privilege tool scope with approval gates are the pre-launch controls; a prompt instruction is not a control.
Data minimisation: only the minimum necessary record content belongs in context.
Instrumentation deferred until after stabilisation is exactly the design-time observability rule being broken.
At scale, structured traces with correlation ids plus sampled and error-triggered payloads beat capture-everything.
Aggregate dashboards and per-request traces answer different questions; the per-request layer is missing.
Many owners, churn, and reuse across applications is the MCP server case.
Three different jobs need three entry points; the architect names the trade-off rather than standardising for consistency.
Two independently operated agents that will not expose internals to each other is the agent-to-agent protocol case.

items.chosen: MCP server | direct API integration | agent-to-agent protocol | MCP server | direct API integration
items.keyed: MCP server | direct API integration | agent-to-agent protocol | MCP server | direct API integration
items.reasoning: Reusable shared access and org-wide discoverability are MCP; no-model batch transfer and a single embedded classification call are direct API; cross-company agents are A2A.
Progressive discovery wins under a constrained context budget and when only a small subset of a large catalogue is relevant per request.
Overlapping tool purposes are fixed by consolidation and explicit non-overlapping boundaries, not by more indirection.
Fixed-size blocks sever defined terms and cross-references; structure-aware chunking with linking metadata restores them.
Exact style codes need lexical matching while natural language needs semantic: hybrid retrieval weighted by query shape.
Validated re-indexing after each refresh plus version metadata filtering superseded records addresses stale answers directly.
Retries with backoff plus fallback, and circuit breakers, are design-time resilience; the rest are post-hoc process.
1.4s p95 plus 500ms stays well under a 3s SLA for a 9-point accuracy gain.
Evals written first define acceptance; written after, they only describe whatever the pipeline does.
A golden set needs expert-labelled edge cases plus a real-distribution sample; self-generated and prompt-borrowed cases are circular.

items.chosen: golden-dataset evaluation | LLM-as-judge with human calibration | canary release with A/B comparison | adversarial test suite | golden-dataset evaluation
items.keyed: golden-dataset evaluation | LLM-as-judge with human calibration | canary release with A/B comparison | adversarial test suite | golden-dataset evaluation
items.reasoning: Regression on agreed cases and upgrade checks on high-risk types are golden-dataset; rubric scoring at volume is judge; tied offline with a pre-fixed metric needs live A/B; tenant-isolation probing is adversarial.
Good enough has to be defined as task metrics tied to business outcomes with agreed launch thresholds.
Subjective quality at volume is the LLM-as-judge case, and calibration against human editors is what makes it trustworthy.
An A/B needs its primary metric and sample size fixed before it runs, or the read is post hoc.
Spot checks are not an eval; run the full suite, then canary gradually with regression monitoring.
Optimise against the measured dominant cost driver rather than assuming the tier is the lever.
A single-site pilot says nothing about group-scale economics; cost and latency must be modelled at full production volume before a public date.
Retrieval relevance decline and rising ungrounded-answer rate lead the user-visible failure; complaints and spend alerts lag.
Pre-production in a regulated domain needs an expert-labelled golden dataset plus an adversarial suite; benchmarks and demos are not evaluation.
Fabricating a certificate number when the tool returned nothing is ungrounded output by definition.
With model, prompt and code unchanged, the causes left are input drift and what the traces of affected sessions show.
Relying on model training for an identity-verification rule means the rule was enforced in no layer of the safety stack.
Only output screening was present; the injected instruction travelled the input and tool-authorisation control points that were never built.
Retrieved contractor content was treated as instruction; retrieved content is data, never instruction-level authority.
Injection cannot be prevented outright, so limit blast radius: least-privilege tools and fail-closed approval on irreversible actions.
No incorrect commitment reaching a borrower needs a blocking output guardrail plus mandatory human approval before sending.

items.chosen: preventative guardrail | human-in-the-loop review | monitoring and audit | preventative guardrail | monitoring and audit
items.keyed: preventative guardrail | human-in-the-loop review | monitoring and audit | preventative guardrail | monitoring and audit
items.reasoning: Never-emit and must-not-display map to preventative guardrails; consequential recommendations to human review; retrospective proof and trend detection to monitoring and audit.
Risk-proportionate gating: approve irreversible or high-impact external actions, let low-risk steps run.
Fairness is a property of the deployed system; prompt framing, routing and thresholds are department-controlled and locally instrumentable.
Postcode is a proxy for protected characteristics; removing explicit fields does not remove the correlation, so evaluate across slices.
Only minimisation/pseudonymisation before the boundary crossing changes what actually leaves; the rest are paperwork or transport controls.
Subprocessor obligations across the data path are architecture-stage and contractual; citation of source records is the strongest rival but is retrofittable.
A requirements-to-paragraph map is not compliance: each control needs a named owner and a living, revalidated evidence artifact.

items.chosen: discovery | design | handoff | monitoring and iteration | discovery
items.keyed: discovery | design | handoff | monitoring and iteration | discovery
items.reasoning: Current-state interviews and success-definition workshops are discovery; retrieval/guardrail selection is design; runbook walkthrough is handoff; eval-trend review is monitoring and iteration.
A stakeholder preference has to be translated into a measurable constraint and carried as a traceable requirement.
Discovery exits on measurable success criteria with thresholds and on a data availability/quality/compliance assessment.
Feasible with constraints, with the heritage boundary documented as load-bearing, is the honest verdict.
Reframe the impossible requirement as measurable acceptance criteria on a probabilistic system.
The architect owns the trade-off presentation including reversal cost; the decision owner decides.
Show the latency breakdown, negotiate an achievable SLA, and use streaming to improve perceived latency.
Signals only act if thresholds come from real sources and each one maps to a trigger action and a named owner.
Infrastructure metrics are not outcomes; report against the discovery success criteria through a translation layer.
Ownership transfers on decisions with rejected alternatives, runbooks and re-runnable eval baselines.
The expansion case rests on the before metric against which improvement is measured and on what the next project can inherit.
Scope changes are assessed against the baseline and re-baselined for cost and risk with sponsor sign-off.
Divergent individual configs are fixed by a shared, version-controlled configuration and standards baseline.
Team setup fixes Skills distribution and model/budget guardrails up front; pilot order and IDE choice are not structural.
A bimodal adoption curve is an enablement gap, worked through champions in batches, not a preference or a licensing question.
Faster merges with fewer comments alongside more incidents is automation bias in review, not tool quality.
Scale safely by constraining what tooling may execute and keeping shared configuration and prompt standards in version control.
Diagnose from traces before changing anything; the prompt-rewrite instinct skips cause identification.
